title: On Curiosity — Sharif Shameem, Lexica
talk_summary: A founder's inspirational talk arguing that curiosity-driven demos are how you discover latent model capabilities, illustrated with historical GPT-3 demos. It contains no engineering mechanisms, measurements, or process techniques—only philosophy and anecdotes.

takeaways.technique: Decompose oversized inputs into a compact 'core essence' before prompting
takeaways.what_they_do: When a web page (~24k tokens) wouldn't fit a 2k-token window, he wrote a custom HTML parser that reduced the page to its essential structure so the model could act on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I wrote a custom HTML parser that would parse a web page into its core essence which was able to fit it into the tiny context window

takeaways.technique: Parallel sub-prompts joined in the background
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the context window couldn't hold a whole app, he split generation into three parallel prompts and merged the outputs afterward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you actually had to do three parallel prompts and then join them in the background

takeaways.what_they_do: The 'Multivac' demo breaks an ambitious goal into sub-problems, then lets you click each sub-idea to decompose further in a visual tree.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you essentially break down the problems into more digestible sub problems and you have this kind of visual interface
